domain_label: Turlock Retail & Goods — Market, Demand & Saturation Economics
purpose: A method for sizing and reading the Turlock independent Retail & Goods market: quantifying the discretionary demand base (a ~72,500 resident, ~$83k-median-income, cost-conscious Central Valley trade area plus CSU Stanislaus and an unusually deep ethnic life-event economy), explaining why the curated catalog of 27 independents saturates internally the way it does (over-built thrift, capex/skill-gated print and sign), mapping competitive structure (crowded vs. white-space) and the leakage that caps the count (Modesto's Vintage Faire Mall, Amazon, online resale, national bridal/jewelry e-tail), and expressing every revenue, margin and market-size figure strictly as a labeled benchmark estimate (industry benchmark x observable size signal) rather than as a stated fact for any named business.
assumptions: no per-business revenue dataset is supplied; every dollar figure is a labeled benchmark estimate, never an actual reported figure for any named independent
the universe is the curated catalog of 27 Turlock Retail & Goods independents in businesses.json (chains excluded), as of the 2026-06-30 snapshot, and that count is treated as a FLOOR not a ceiling
city/county/state figures (population, income, demographics, license fees, the C-45 bond, secondhand-dealer rules) are cited public facts or explicitly labeled derivations

sub-category revenue bands are published industry benchmarks (revenue per store / per employee / markup ratio) scaled DOWN by an observable Turlock size signal (format, footprint, incumbency, headcount), tagged estimate-not-actual with a confidence level and a confirmation path
Modesto (Vintage Faire Mall, big-box, department and chain jewelry, ~15 minutes north) is the single largest leakage sink and the main force capping the apparel-boutique and gift counts
the single highest-leverage confirmation for the uncertain dollar figures is CDTFA / Turlock Finance retail sales-tax receipts split by sub-category
exclusions: per-sub-category sourcing, distributor links, equipment capex and staffing operations — covered by the supply-chain KB
per-sub-category unit-economics, cost-structure and go/no-go business-model detail — covered by the business-models KB (kb1_retail_goods_models)
any claim of an actual, reported, or audited dollar revenue for a named independent
chain and franchise retailers (Vintage Faire tenants, big-box, chain jewelry), which are outside the independents-only catalog
individual merchandising, pricing tactics, or marketing execution for a specific operator
source_description: labeled benchmark estimates and cited public facts for the Turlock independent Retail & Goods market, grounded in the retail_goods deep-dive (DEEPDIVE.md), its reconciled brief (reconciled.md), and the 27-business source dataset (businesses.json); demand sizing uses census population/income and ACS household counts, sub-category revenue bands use published florist/jewelry/bridal/apparel/screen-print/signage/thrift/antique-mall benchmarks scaled to small-market size signals, and saturation/leakage reads use census population and national store-per-capita figures alongside a qualitative Modesto/Amazon/online-resale leakage map
source_citation: Census QuickFacts / California-Demographics / Point2Homes (Turlock ~72,500 pop, ~$82,995 median HH income, ~25,365 households, ~46% Hispanic / ~42% White / ~6% Asian); CSU Stanislaus enrollment (~8,455, Fall 2024, Turlock Journal); KQED / Statistical Atlas (Assyrian ~20k ESTIMATE, Portuguese/Azorean ~7%); IBISWorld (Florists, Bridal Stores, Custom Screen Printing, Small Specialty Retail); National Jeweler / AnythingResearch (jewelry); Sharpsheets (printing/signage); B2B Reviews (US retail store counts); CSLB C-45 classification & $15,000 bond; CDTFA seller's permit; Shopify/Toast/NRF retail cost benchmarks; retail_goods DEEPDIVE.md, reconciled.md, businesses.json

competency_questions.question: What discretionary demand base feeds Turlock's Retail & Goods spending, how large is the resident trade area, and why does this sector lack the necessity floor that cushions food or auto retail?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: DEMAND_BASE names the ~72,500 residents at ~$83k median income across ~25,365 households plus CSU Stanislaus, and states the sector is overwhelmingly discretionary with no third-party-payer or reimbursement buffer, tagged with source confidence

competency_questions.question: How does Turlock's ethnic life-event economy raise the sustainable independent count above what middling income alone would predict?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: ETHNIC_EVENT_DEMAND ties the Assyrian (~20k ESTIMATE), Portuguese/Azorean (~7%), Mexican-origin and Punjabi/Sikh communities to the formalwear, florist, jewelry and custom-print formats their culture-heavy event calendars sustain, and explains the load-bearing demand floor

competency_questions.question: Why are the defended event categories (bridal, fine jewelry, sympathy florals) capped by annual event volume rather than by store count?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: EVENT_VOLUME_CEILING explains that weddings, engagements and funerals form a fixed annual transaction pool, so a naive second store splits share rather than growing the market

competency_questions.question: Why is the curated 27-business catalog a coverage FLOOR, and how does that caveat propagate into every saturation and white-space read?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: COVERAGE_FLOOR states the catalog counts independents only, that uncatalogued home-based sellers, booth dealers and pop-ups push the true count to at least 27 and plausibly higher, and that ~9 of 27 entries are med/low confidence

competency_questions.question: How is the ~3.7-per-10,000 independent-specialty saturation density built, and why is it modest rather than saturated against the right comparator?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: SATURATION_DENSITY derives 27 / (72,500/10,000) = ~3.7 per 10k, contrasts it with the ~128-175 total-retail figure (which includes grocery/big-box/auto/chains), and reads the independent-specialty slice as modest, propped up by ethnic-event demand

competency_questions.question: How is a per-sub-category benchmark revenue band built so it is an honest estimate and never a stated fact for a named business?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: BENCHMARK_REVENUE_BANDS states the benchmark x size-signal method, gives the per-sub-category bands (florist $180k-$450k, jewelry $350k-$900k, bridal $300k-$900k, thrift $60k-$300k, used books $30k-$150k, etc.), and tags every band estimate-not-actual with confidence and a confirmation path

competency_questions.question: Why does high gross margin in thrift and antiques not mean high profit, and where does the margin reality bite?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: MARGIN_REALITY explains the thrift high-gross/thin-net paradox (near-zero donated COGS but highest sorting labor, foot-traffic-capped low-ticket revenue, intense resale competition) and the antique-mall landlord economics (booth rent + commission, not inventory ownership)

competency_questions.question: Why does Turlock's Retail & Goods sector saturate internally the lopsided way it does — over-built at the easy end, thin at the hard end — rather than at a uniform density?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: INTERNAL_LOPSIDEDNESS explains the asymmetry: the no-capital, no-license thrift format over-builds (5 of 27) while capex/skill-gated custom-print and sign stay thin despite demand headroom

competency_questions.question: Which sub-categories are crowded by intra-Turlock competition and which are genuine white-space, once secondary-category straddles are folded in?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: COMPETITIVE_STRUCTURE gives a per-sub-category crowded/white-space read (thrift over-built; florist/jewelry crowded by count but low head-to-head; antiques partly aggregated by Main Street Antiques; custom-print/sign white-space) and notes how secondaries make Gifts and Jewelry less thin

competency_questions.question: How does the capex and skilled-labor moat gate entry into the operationally hard formats independently of demand?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: CAPEX_SKILL_GATE names the wide-format/CNC and screen-print/DTG capex, the bench-jeweler/tailor/C-45-installer skilled-labor constraint and the $15,000 C-45 bond, and explains why white-space in print/sign is hard to capture rather than easy upside

competency_questions.question: How does demand leak out of Turlock, and how are the leakage sinks ranked?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: LEAKAGE_MAP ranks Modesto/Vintage Faire (largest), Amazon/online (forced Lightly Used Books offline in 2025), online resale (Poshmark/ThredUp/eBay vs thrift), Bay Area/Monterey outlets, and national bridal/jewelry e-tail, flagging it an estimate of cross-shopping behavior

competency_questions.question: How is a go/no-go market verdict reached for adding a Retail & Goods format, what binding constraint flips by category, and how are the reads refreshed when the underlying figures change?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: MARKET_GO_NOGO produces a verdict combining the saturation read, the crowded/white-space structure, the leakage exposure and the capex/skill gate (refusing a sixth thrift, a fourth antiques, or a naive second bridal generalist; allowing only differentiated/gated openings), diagnosing whether the binding wall is demand+leakage or capex+labor, and MARKET_REVIEW_LOOP defines the refresh triggers (new CDTFA data, a catalog open/close, a demographic or enrollment refresh, a fee/bond change) that re-run the sizing and saturation reads

glossary.definition: Turlock's ~72,500-resident, ~$83k-median-income, ~25,365-household base whose Retail & Goods spending is overwhelmingly discretionary (no necessity floor, no insurance or third-party-payer buffer), making the whole sector cyclically exposed in a way a necessity sector is not.

Turlock's load-bearing demand floor: deep Assyrian (~20k, ESTIMATE), Portuguese/Azorean (~7%), Mexican-origin and Punjabi/Sikh communities whose culture-heavy weddings, quinceaneras, festivals and sacraments drive repeat demand for formalwear, florals, gold-gifting jewelry and custom print, sustaining formats a same-size generic town could not.

The cap on the defended categories (bridal, fine jewelry, sympathy florals) set by the fixed annual number of weddings, engagements and funerals in the trade area, not by store count; a naive second store splits a fixed transaction pool rather than growing the market.

The rule that the curated 27-business catalog counts independents only and is a lower bound; uncatalogued home-based sellers, the 28+ booth dealers inside Main Street Antiques, and pop-ups mean the true independent count is at least 27 and plausibly higher, so every white-space read is a floor read.

The saturation read 27 / (72,500 / 10,000) = ~3.7 independents per 10,000 residents, measuring only the independent specialty slice (not the ~128-175 total-retail figure that includes grocery, big-box, auto, gas and chains), read as modest rather than saturated.

The honest revenue-estimation method: take a published per-store / per-employee / markup industry benchmark and scale it DOWN by an observable Turlock size signal (format, footprint, incumbency, headcount), yielding a band tagged estimate-not-actual with a confidence level and confirmation path.

The high-gross/thin-net reality of donated-goods thrift: gross margin on donated inventory is high (near-zero COGS) but net margin is squeezed by the sector's highest sorting labor, foot-traffic-capped low-ticket revenue, and intense regional/online resale competition; high gross never means high profit here.

Turlock's defining structure: aggregate density is modest (~3.7/10k) but the easy/no-capital thrift format over-builds (5 of 27) while operationally hard, capex/skill-gated custom-print and sign formats stay thin despite genuine demand headroom.

The equipment and skilled-labor moat that gates the operationally hard formats independently of demand: wide-format/CNC and screen-print/DTG capex, bench-jeweler/tailor/C-45-installer labor scarcity, and the $15,000 CSLB C-45 sign-contractor bond — the reason print/sign white-space is hard to capture, not easy upside.

A destination that pulls discretionary demand out of Turlock, ranked: Modesto's Vintage Faire Mall and big-box/chain jewelry (largest), Amazon/online, online resale (Poshmark/ThredUp/eBay), Bay Area/Monterey outlets, and national bridal/jewelry e-tail; the largest single force capping the sector's count.

nodes.definition: Catalog the discretionary demand engine that feeds Turlock's Retail & Goods spending: a ~72,500-resident base (2024 est. ~72,502) with a ~$82,995 median household income across ~25,365 households averaging ~3 persons, plus ~8,455 CSU Stanislaus students. This is a solidly middle-income but cost-conscious Central Valley base, well below coastal California, with high price sensitivity for everyday apparel and gifts. Critically the whole sector is overwhelmingly discretionary: with the narrow exceptions of sympathy florals and B2B sign/print, nothing here is a weekly necessity, and there is no insurance or third-party-reimbursement buffer of the kind that cushions health or auto retail. That single fact makes revenue track local discretionary income and consumer confidence, leaving the sector cyclically exposed in a way Food & Dining's necessity floor is not.

nodes.definition: Isolate the cap on the defended event categories: bridal, fine jewelry and sympathy florals are limited by the annual number of weddings, engagements and funerals in the trade area, not by store count. This is the mechanism behind the sector's strongest moat and its sharpest entry trap simultaneously. The ethnic-event economy props the demand for these categories up, but the transaction pool is fixed per year, so adding a naive second bridal store or a fourth jeweler splits a fixed pool rather than growing the market. White-space in these categories exists only if a second entrant specializes (e.g., Hispanic-formalwear) or pulls destination demand from bridal-less surrounding Stanislaus/Merced towns; the incumbent's trunk-show and Jim's Formal Wear relationships and special-order lead times favor it against a generalist challenger.

nodes.definition: Build the saturation number as a labeled estimate: curated independent count / (population / 10,000) = 27 / 7.25 = ~3.7 independent Retail & Goods businesses per 10,000 residents (the numerator is a curated independents-only catalog; high confidence on the count itself, medium that it is exhaustive; this is a FLOOR). nodes.definition: Correct the most consequential margin misread: high gross margin does not mean high profit, most sharply in thrift and antiques. Donated-goods thrift (Charity Thrift, DIGS, Little Red Door, Off Center, Vintage Thrift) shows high gross margin on near-zero-COGS donated inventory, yet net margin is squeezed by the sector's highest sorting labor, foot-traffic-capped low-ticket revenue, and intense regional Goodwill/Salvation Army and online-resale competition. Separately, the multi-dealer antiques mall (Main Street Antiques, 28+ dealers) is one destination, not four rivals, and runs landlord-plus-checkout economics: revenue is booth rent (~$1-$2/sq ft/mo) plus ~10-40% sales commission plus 2-4% card fees, not inventory ownership — a fundamentally different P&L from the solo vintage shops (Treasure Hunters, Vintage Market, Studio A) it shares a category with. Typical independent-retail net margin runs ~3-13%; rent (5-15% of revenue) is the swing variable and no actual Turlock rent figure was sourced.

nodes.definition: Explain the sector's defining structure: aggregate density is modest (~3.7/10k), but the internal distribution is lopsided, and this asymmetry — not the aggregate — is the real story. The easy format (thrift — near-zero capital, no inventory cost, no license moat) over-builds at 5 of 27, the single largest sub-category, while the operationally hard formats with genuine demand headroom (custom print at 1 primary, sign at 2) stay thin because few operators can clear the equipment/skill barrier. The market lens treats entry as purely demand-capped; the supply lens adds the second constraint — a skilled-labor and capex moat — so the corollary is that low-barrier formats fill in to (and past) their demand while high-barrier formats leave demand un-served. The whole structure is held together by culture-driven event demand rather than by income, which is only middling and leaks heavily.

nodes.definition: Give the per-sub-category competitive read, separating crowded intra-Turlock competition from genuine white-space. Crowded: thrift/consignment (5 — the single largest, lowest-entry-cost format, competing with each other, regional Goodwill/Salvation Army and online resale — do not add a sixth); florist (3) and jewelry (3) crowded by count but with low head-to-head substitution (the jewelers split repair / fine-custom / legacy niches; florists defended by sympathy/event inelasticity); antiques/vintage (4) crowded but partly aggregated because Main Street Antiques functions as one destination not four rivals. White-space: custom apparel/print (1 primary) the clearest expansion lane but capex/skill-gated; sign/print (2) the highest-barrier version (C-45 bond + wide-format/CNC); men's/bridal (1 each) near-monopoly but capped by event volume; gifts/specialty (1 primary) thin but Amazon-exposed and hazardous. A taxonomy caveat: folding in secondary-category straddles (Bijou, Rustic Roots, California Couture, D2, Off Center) makes Gifts and Jewelry materially less thin than the primary-only count suggests.

nodes.definition: Define the supply-side entry gate the demand view alone misses: for most of the sector capex is low (fixtures, cases, a POS, fitting rooms) and the barrier is inventory working capital and demand, but three sub-categories are genuinely capex/skill-gated, which makes their white-space hard to capture rather than easy upside. Sign/print is highest: a wide-format printer, CNC router and plotter (54-inch latex ~$7.5k, UV flatbed ~$55k — ESTIMATE list prices) plus the CSLB C-45 sign-contractor license, which requires 4 years journeyman experience, an exam, and a $15,000 contractor bond — the single hardest licensing gate in the sector (Posted; J&J for installed/illuminated signs). Jewelry and custom home-decor build are med (bench tools, laser welder, CAD, a safe; woodshop and refinishing). nodes.definition: Account for the second force capping the count: middling, cost-conscious discretionary income. nodes.definition: Read the sector not as one model but four, each with a different cost spine that governs how its revenue band converts to profit. (1) Buy-for-resale (apparel, gifts, decor, jewelry — Bella Forte, Glitz, Bijou, D2, the three jewelers): capital tied up in inventory, operating risk is markdown / aging stock not perishability. (2) Perishable just-in-time (florists — De La Fleur, Flowers By Eva, Yonan's Floral): the only true JIT/cold-chain operation, shrink risk is the defining cost, labor design- and delivery-heavy. (3) Substrate + conversion (sign/print, custom apparel, custom furniture — J&J, Posted, Crivelli's, D2, Rustic Roots): blank goods converted in-house with capex equipment, B2B-leaning manufacturers as much as retailers, cost spine is equipment depreciation + skilled operator/install labor. (4) Acquisition-sourced (thrift, antiques, used books — the five thrift stores, Main Street Antiques, Lightly Used Books): essentially no upstream distributor, COGS is donations, estate buys, consignor splits, dealer booth rent — lowest-COGS, highest-sorting-labor model. Which model a format belongs to determines whether its binding constraint is inventory, shrink, capex, or sorting labor.

included: the four cost-spine models and which businesses fall in each

pros.example: a florist's shrink risk and a thrift's sorting labor are different binding constraints behind similar low bands

cons.example: D2 is both buy-for-resale decor and substrate-conversion custom furniture

failure_modes: applying one model's binding constraint to a format in a different model
ignoring that straddle businesses carry two cost spines
acceptance_tests: the four cost-spine models are each named with example businesses and their distinct binding constraint (inventory, shrink, capex, sorting labor)
revisit_triggers: a business changes its dominant model
a new format that does not fit the four models appears
a cost-spine benchmark updates

base.update_signal: a business's dominant cost model changes

nodes.definition: Account for the demand peaks an annual revenue band averages away, which are sharpest in exactly the culture-anchored categories and create event-surge labor needs invisible in a flat band. Formal/bridal/tux/menswear ride the sector's strongest event calendar: prom (spring), wedding season (May-Oct), quinceanera and holiday (winter). Florists peak at Valentine's Day, Mother's Day, weddings (spring-fall) and holidays, with non-seasonal funerals and same-day delivery as a differentiator (Flowers By Eva). Gifts/decor/jewelry concentrate in Q4 holiday plus Valentine's (jewelry) and Mother's Day. Sign/print is B2B and counter-cyclical to consumer seasons, tied to local business openings and events. The labor model is structurally owner-operator + small crew with sharp event-driven surges, so an operator who reads only the annual band will mis-plan both cash flow and staffing through the peaks and troughs.

nodes.definition: Separate the formats under structural online pressure from those defended against it, using the leakage map overlaid on format economics. Most pressured: used books (the lowest-margin format, already migrated — Lightly Used Books closed its physical store in March 2025 and is online-only, the local signature of Amazon leakage); gifts/specialty (the format most exposed to Amazon, so its thinness is hazardous not inviting); commodity/basic apparel (leaks to Amazon and Modesto). Pressured but partly defended: thrift/consignment (faces online resale via Poshmark/ThredUp/eBay but retains a treasure-hunt and donation-economics moat). Most defended: the event categories — bridal, fine jewelry, sympathy florals — where local fit, service, and the ethnic-wedding/gold-gifting economy provide the strongest moat in the sector against national bridal/jewelry e-tail; and B2B sign/print, which is contract-driven and less cyclical. The trajectory read is directional, not a measured share shift.

nodes.definition: Read the defensibility that deep-rooted incumbency confers on the established formats, a moat a new-entrant demand read alone misses. Several catalog members are decades-old institutions: J & J Printing (since 1975), Camara's Clothier (40+ years), Glitz (since 2005), Flowers By Eva (25+ years), Vail Creek (22+ years), and Yonan's Jewelers ('Turlock's oldest family-owned jewelry store, three generations'). The recurring Yonan's name across both Florist and Jewelry reflects the Assyrian family-business density that defines much of Turlock's retail fabric. Incumbency compounds the moats already described: trunk-show and Jim's Formal Wear relationships (Camara's), bench-skill and memo-financing reputation (the jewelers), and event-calendar referral networks (the florists) make a generalist challenger's entry harder than a count of one or three implies. This is why the near-monopoly and crowded-by-count categories resist new entry even where the event economy looks to support more — the incumbent owns the relationships, not just the storefront.

nodes.definition: Locate and rank the defensible white-space — sub-categories where both demand and operations permit entry — and mark each viable only after its cost gate clears, because demand headroom and entry difficulty are two different things. Ranked: (1) custom apparel/print — the clearest expansion lane given the large Hispanic/Assyrian/Portuguese festival, church and event-apparel calendar, but capturable only by an operator who can clear the equipment + screen-print/DTG operator-skill barrier; (2) sign/print — the strongest version of the same pattern and the highest-barrier white-space (C-45 $15k bond + wide-format/CNC capex), real under-served B2B demand but gated hard; (3) a specialized formalwear concept (Hispanic-formalwear or destination-bridal pulling bridal-less surrounding towns) — room exists only for a differentiated entrant, never a naive generalist that splits the fixed event pool. nodes.definition: Define the regulatory gates, whose defining fact is that the barrier to entry is low for most of the sector — demand, not licensing, is the cap — with occupational-licensing moats existing only in narrow slices. Cited public facts: a CDTFA seller's permit (sales tax) is required of all 27 and is free; a City of Turlock business license plus zoning/use permit applies (downtown storefront use permits included); the CSLB C-45 sign-contractor license gates sign installation/electrical (Posted; J&J for installed/illuminated signs), requiring 4 years journeyman experience, an exam, and a $15,000 contractor bond — the single hardest licensing gate. Labeled estimates: a CSLB contractor license may apply to custom furniture install once a job exceeds the $500 labor-and-materials threshold (D2, Rustic Roots); buying gold/precious metal from the public (Universal, Yonan's) typically triggers secondhand-dealer / precious-metals registration plus police reporting and hold periods; thrift/used-book resale can trigger secondhand-dealer registration. Jewelers add jewelers-block insurance; florists/sign shops add auto for delivery/install vehicles.

nodes.definition: Read Turlock against its regional context: it anchors the southern half of Stanislaus County (~552k county population) and can pull destination demand from smaller, format-less surrounding Stanislaus/Merced towns even as it leaks mid-tier browsing up to Modesto. This two-way flow is the structural nuance behind the white-space reads: surrounding rural towns lacking bridal, formalwear or jewelry formats give a differentiated Turlock entrant a destination-demand draw that pure resident math misses, while Modesto's larger scene caps Turlock's own mid-tier apparel and gift ceiling. The pull is strongest for the high-consideration, infrequent event purchase (a gown, a ring) where a shopper will travel, and weakest for commodity gifts and basic apparel that leak the other way to Modesto and Amazon. Magnitudes are estimates of cross-shopping behavior, not measured figures; a trade-area capture study would confirm.

nodes.definition: Produce the market go/no-go verdict for adding a given Retail & Goods format, composing the saturation density, the crowded/white-space structure, the leakage exposure, the online-pressure trajectory, and the capex/skill and regulatory gates into one decision. The merged rule: do not add a sixth thrift store, a fourth antiques shop, or a naive second bridal/formalwear generalist (these over-build the easy end or split a fixed event pool); the defensible headroom is custom apparel/print, sign/print, and a specialized formalwear concept (Hispanic-formalwear or destination-bridal pulling surrounding towns) — each viable only after clearing its cost gate (capex + operator skill for print/sign, the C-45 bond for sign install, a differentiation/destination strategy for formalwear). The binding constraint flips by category: for thrift/gifts/apparel it is demand and leakage; for print/sign/jewelry it is capex and skilled-labor supply. An entrant must diagnose which wall they actually face before assuming white-space means easy. A demand-true opening that fails its cost gate is a no-go until the gate clears.

the heritage family-business incumbency is a refinement of the ethnic-event demand into durable owner relationships
incumbency reads which crowded-by-count or near-monopoly categories are defended beyond raw store count
the verdict debits an incumbent's relationship moat against a generalist challenger's apparent headroom

conflict_axes.name: demand_headroom_vs_capex_skill_gate
conflict_axes.description: A format can be demand-true white space yet be walled off by equipment capex, operator skill, or the C-45 bond, so the demand and feasibility views point opposite ways.
poles: block on the unmet capex/skill gate
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: treat a demand-true opening as a no-go until its capex/skill and C-45 gate clears; demand never overrides the supply-side moat

conflict_axes.name: high_gross_vs_thin_net
conflict_axes.description: Donated-COGS thrift and landlord-economics antiques show high gross margin that does not survive into net profit once sorting labor, low-ticket foot traffic and rent are counted.
poles: anchor to the thin net margin
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: always pair a high-gross band with its thin-net caveat; high gross never means high profit, most sharply for thrift

conflict_axes.name: modest_aggregate_vs_lopsided_internal
conflict_axes.description: The ~3.7/10k aggregate density reads modest while the internal distribution is lopsided (over-built thrift, thin print/sign), so the aggregate and the internal reads imply opposite entry conclusions.
poles: read the modest aggregate as room
read the lopsided internal as format-specific
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: the aggregate is modest but never an invitation to add anywhere; entry is governed by the format-specific lopsided read

conflict_axes.name: ethnic_event_floor_vs_leakage_ceiling
conflict_axes.description: The ethnic life-event economy props the count up above income prediction while Modesto/Amazon/online-resale leakage pulls discretionary demand away and caps it.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: the event economy raises the floor for defended event/owner-operated formats; leakage caps the mid-tier apparel/gift formats; apply each to the formats it governs

conflict_axes.name: online_pressure_vs_local_event_durability
conflict_axes.description: Online leakage signals (books offline, gifts Amazon-exposed) can mislabel durable local event formats that national e-tail does not erode.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: apply online pressure to commodity/undifferentiated formats; discount it for event categories defended by local fit and the ethnic-wedding economy

conflict_axes.name: annual_band_vs_event_surge_concentration
conflict_axes.description: A flat annual revenue band averages away the prom/wedding/quinceanera and Q4-holiday peaks that drive working-capital and event-surge labor risk.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: always pair the annual band with the format's event-surge seasonal profile before any cash-flow or staffing read

conflict_axes.name: resident_count_vs_two_way_destination_pull
conflict_axes.description: Sizing on Turlock residents alone misses both the inbound destination draw from smaller towns and the outbound leakage to Modesto, which point opposite ways for different formats.
poles: size on the two-way cross-shop flow
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: credit surrounding-town draw to differentiated event formats and debit Modesto leakage from mid-tier apparel/gift, rather than reading a single resident pool

conflict_axes.name: estimate_labeling_vs_decisiveness
conflict_axes.description: Rigorous estimate-not-actual labeling protects honesty but can make the analysis read as too hedged to act on.
poles: label every figure as an estimate
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: label every figure but pair it with a confidence and a CDTFA confirmation path so the read stays actionable without overclaiming

conflict_axes.name: snapshot_stability_vs_online_drift
conflict_axes.description: The ~27-count, ~3.7/10k snapshot reads as stable, but advancing online leakage (one bookstore already offline) and uncatalogued entrants are moving the underlying structure.
poles: track the online and coverage drift
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: hold the snapshot as a dated floor baseline but let the review loop, not assumption, decide when online drift or a new entrant has moved the structure

edge_cases.description: The ~3.7-per-10k independent-specialty density is compared against the ~128-175 total-retail headline and read as gross under-supply
edge_cases.trigger: the independent-specialty figure is benchmarked against the wrong total-retail comparator
edge_cases.mitigation: compare only against the independent-specialty subset and read ~3.7 as modest-not-saturated, not against the chain-inclusive 128-175 figure

edge_cases.description: A sub-category revenue band is attached to a named business as if it were that business's actual revenue
edge_cases.trigger: a per-sub-category estimate is quoted next to a specific operator's name
edge_cases.mitigation: keep every band sub-category-level and estimate-not-actual; never bind a dollar figure to a named business as fact

edge_cases.description: A high-gross thrift or donated-goods format is read as high-profit
edge_cases.trigger: near-zero donated COGS is taken as net margin without the labor and foot-traffic cap
edge_cases.mitigation: pair the high gross with the highest-sorting-labor, low-ticket, resale-competition thin-net reality

edge_cases.description: A demand-true custom-print or sign opening is recommended without pricing the capex and C-45 gate
edge_cases.trigger: a print/sign white-space is judged on demand headroom alone
edge_cases.mitigation: apply the wide-format/CNC capex and the $15,000 C-45 bond as an override before any print/sign yes

edge_cases.description: A naive second bridal or formalwear generalist is recommended because event demand looks strong
edge_cases.trigger: strong ethnic-event demand is read as headroom for a duplicate generalist
edge_cases.mitigation: treat the event pool as fixed-per-year; allow only a specialized (Hispanic-formalwear) or destination-pull entrant, never a generalist share-splitter

edge_cases.description: A singleton white-space category is read as confirmed absence when uncatalogued entrants may occupy it
edge_cases.trigger: a primary-only count of 1 is taken as a verified open lane
edge_cases.mitigation: read every singleton as a floor; fold in secondary straddles (Gifts via Bijou/California Couture/D2/Off Center) and flag possible uncatalogued entrants

edge_cases.description: An event-concentrated business is sized on a flat annual band
edge_cases.trigger: an annual revenue band is used for cash-flow or staffing planning without the event-surge profile
edge_cases.mitigation: overlay the format's event-surge peaks (prom/wedding/quinceanera, Q4 holiday, Valentine's) on the annual band before any working-capital or staffing read

edge_cases.description: Modesto/Amazon leakage logic is applied to the defended event categories the ethnic-wedding economy protects
edge_cases.trigger: the apparel/gift leakage map is extended to bridal, fine jewelry or sympathy florals
edge_cases.mitigation: apply leakage to commodity/mid-tier formats and credit local fit + the ethnic-wedding/gold-gifting moat to the defended event categories

edge_cases.description: The Assyrian ~20,000 magnitude is quoted as a bare Census FACT
edge_cases.trigger: the 'quarter of the city' community figure is stated without the ESTIMATE tag
edge_cases.mitigation: carry the Assyrian magnitude as a labeled ESTIMATE (press/community estimate), never a bare FACT lead

edge_cases.description: The multi-dealer antiques mall is counted as four rivals and sized on solo-shop inventory economics
edge_cases.trigger: Main Street Antiques (28+ dealers) is tallied and modeled like the solo vintage shops
edge_cases.mitigation: treat the mall as one destination on landlord (booth-rent + commission) economics, distinct from the solo shops in its category

edge_cases.description: CDTFA retail sales-tax receipts arrive and contradict the estimated bands and density
edge_cases.mitigation: fire the review loop, replace the band/density/distribution estimates with the measured figures, and re-derive the reads

workflow.description: Record the resident base, median income, household count and CSU enrollment with cited magnitudes and the no-necessity-floor caveat
workflow.gate: the resident base, income and household count each have a public-fact magnitude and the discretionary character is stated

workflow.description: Tie each heritage community to the event formats its culture-heavy calendar anchors, with the Assyrian figure tagged ESTIMATE
workflow.gate: each of the four communities is tied to an anchored event format with its share and the demand-floor role is stated

workflow.description: State the catalog as independents-only and a lower bound, naming under-captured entrant types and the med/low-confidence entries
workflow.gate: the catalog is stated as a floor and the ~9-of-27 med/low-confidence entries are flagged

workflow.description: Compute 27 / (72,500/10,000) = ~3.7 per 10k and contrast it with the wrong total-retail comparator
workflow.gate: the ~3.7-per-10k figure is derived, the 128-175 comparator is excluded, and the modest-not-saturated floor read is stated

workflow.description: Derive each band as a national benchmark scaled by a size signal, paired with its margin caveat and CDTFA confirmation
workflow.gate: every band is estimate-not-actual with a size signal, confidence, and margin pairing

workflow.description: State the thrift high-gross/thin-net paradox and the antique-mall landlord economics
workflow.gate: the high-gross/thin-net paradox and the landlord-vs-solo-shop distinction are stated

workflow.action: Read the internal lopsidedness and competitive structure
workflow.description: Set each sub-category's count against a crowded or white-space read, noting straddles and the antiques aggregation
workflow.gate: each major sub-category has a crowded/white-space read consistent with the lopsided structure

workflow.action: Price the capex/skill and regulatory gate
workflow.description: Name the wide-format/CNC and screen-print capex, the skilled-labor scarcity and the C-45 $15k bond
workflow.gate: the print/sign capex, the C-45 bond and the bench-labor constraint are each stated as the supply-side moat

workflow.description: Rank leakage sinks and the defensible openings, marking each viable only after its cost gate clears
workflow.gate: leakage sinks are ranked and three+ openings are ranked, each with a demand basis and a cost-gate qualifier

workflow.description: Combine saturation, competitive structure, leakage and the cost gate into an add/avoid call diagnosing the binding wall
workflow.gate: the verdict refuses any demand-true but cost-gated addition and names the do-not-add formats

workflow.action: Set the market review cadence and triggers
workflow.description: Define the refresh cadence and material-change triggers routing back to density and the revenue bands
workflow.gate: a cadence and a trigger list (CDTFA highest-leverage) routing to SATURATION_DENSITY and the bands exist

dominance_rules.rule: The revenue-honesty guardrail dominates any pressure for a single decisive number
dominance_rules.rationale: no per-business revenue is public, so an over-decisive figure would be a fabrication
dominance_rules.trigger: a request for a named business's revenue or a single market number
dominance_rules.action: answer only with a labeled estimate (benchmark x size signal) plus confidence and the CDTFA confirmation path

dominance_rules.rule: The capex/skill gate dominates a demand-true white-space opening
dominance_rules.rationale: equipment capex, operator skill and the C-45 bond can make a high-demand format un-capturable
dominance_rules.trigger: a print/sign or other hard-format opening is judged on demand alone
dominance_rules.action: mark it a no-go until the capex/skill and C-45 cost gate clears

dominance_rules.rule: The thin-net caveat dominates a high-gross revenue band
dominance_rules.rationale: donated-COGS thrift and landlord-economics antiques show high gross that does not survive into net
dominance_rules.trigger: a high-gross format is read as high-profit
dominance_rules.action: pair the band with its highest-sorting-labor / low-ticket / rent thin-net reality before any profit read

dominance_rules.rule: Local event durability dominates online-pressure decline for defended event formats
dominance_rules.rationale: national bridal/jewelry e-tail does not erode the locally-fit, ethnic-wedding-anchored event categories
dominance_rules.trigger: an online-decline signal is applied to bridal, fine jewelry or sympathy florals
dominance_rules.action: discount the online trajectory for event categories with durable local fit and the gold-gifting/wedding economy

dominance_rules.rule: The event-volume ceiling dominates demand math for the defended event categories
dominance_rules.rationale: a fixed annual transaction pool caps bridal/jewelry/florist regardless of how strong demand looks
dominance_rules.trigger: a second generalist event store is justified on strong demand alone
dominance_rules.action: cap the category at its fixed event pool and allow only a specialized or destination entrant

dominance_rules.rule: The event-surge seasonal profile dominates the annual band for cash-flow and staffing reads
dominance_rules.rationale: a flat annual band hides the prom/wedding/quinceanera and Q4 peaks that drive working-capital and surge-labor risk
dominance_rules.trigger: an annual band is used for a cash-flow or staffing decision
dominance_rules.action: overlay the format's event-surge seasonal profile before deciding

dominance_rules.rule: The coverage-floor read dominates a singleton white-space conclusion
dominance_rules.rationale: a primary-only count of 1 can hide secondary straddles and uncatalogued entrants
dominance_rules.trigger: a singleton category is read as a confirmed open lane
dominance_rules.action: fold in straddles and treat the singleton as a floor, not a confirmed absence

dominance_rules.rule: The right independent-specialty comparator dominates the total-retail headline in the density read
dominance_rules.rationale: the 128-175 total-retail figure includes grocery, big-box, auto and chains and is the wrong comparator
dominance_rules.trigger: the ~3.7 independent-specialty density is compared to the chain-inclusive headline
dominance_rules.action: compare only against the independent-specialty subset and read ~3.7 as modest-not-saturated

dominance_rules.rule: A flagged low-confidence input dominates a confident downstream conclusion built on it
dominance_rules.rationale: a conclusion cannot be more certain than its weakest load-bearing input
dominance_rules.trigger: a benchmark band or the leakage estimate carries a conclusion above its own confidence
dominance_rules.action: cap the conclusion's confidence at that of its weakest input and name the CDTFA or cross-shop confirmation source

anti_rework_rules.rule: Establish the coverage floor and density before reading saturation or white-space
anti_rework_rules.prevents: a saturation conclusion built on a count later revealed as a soft floor, forcing a re-read

anti_rework_rules.rule: Label every dollar figure estimate-not-actual at the moment it is written
anti_rework_rules.prevents: a later honesty sweep that must re-caveat figures already quoted as facts

anti_rework_rules.rule: Read competitive structure off primary category, folding in secondary straddles, before counting
anti_rework_rules.prevents: double-counted or single-counted straddle formats inflating or deflating a read that must be re-tallied

anti_rework_rules.rule: Apply the capex/skill and C-45 gate while ranking white-space, not after recommending it
anti_rework_rules.prevents: recommending a print/sign or other hard opening that the equipment/bond gate then voids

anti_rework_rules.rule: Pair every high-gross band with its thin-net caveat when the band is built
anti_rework_rules.prevents: a high-gross-equals-profit read that must be reworked once the cost spine is surfaced

anti_rework_rules.rule: Attach the event-surge seasonal profile to a format's band when the band is built
anti_rework_rules.prevents: a flat-band cash-flow or staffing plan that must be reworked once the peaks are surfaced

anti_rework_rules.rule: Tag the Assyrian magnitude and equipment list prices ESTIMATE the first time they are stated
anti_rework_rules.prevents: every downstream use inheriting an unflagged figure that must later be re-tagged

anti_rework_rules.rule: Name the CDTFA confirmation path on every low-confidence dollar figure as it is stated
anti_rework_rules.prevents: a later pass to attach confirmation sources to numbers already published without them

anti_rework_rules.rule: Diagnose whether the binding wall is demand+leakage or capex+labor before judging a format's headroom
anti_rework_rules.prevents: a white-space-means-easy conclusion that must be reversed once the real binding constraint is identified

iteration_protocol.trigger: CDTFA / Turlock Finance retail sales-tax receipts split by sub-category become available
iteration_protocol.action: replace the revenue bands, the density read and the per-business distribution estimates with measured figures and re-derive

iteration_protocol.trigger: a census/ACS demographic or CSU enrollment refresh lands
iteration_protocol.action: re-run the demand base and ethnic-event demand and re-derive the density

iteration_protocol.trigger: a format opens or closes in the catalog or a confidence flag is upgraded
iteration_protocol.action: re-tally the coverage floor, the saturation reads and the competitive structure

iteration_protocol.trigger: an online-retail or online-resale share shift, or another format migrates online
iteration_protocol.action: refresh the leakage map and the online-pressure trajectory and re-rank white-space

iteration_protocol.trigger: a city/county/CSLB permit, license, or C-45-bond fee or rule changes
iteration_protocol.action: re-price the capex/skill and regulatory gate and re-issue any affected go/no-go verdicts

iteration_protocol.trigger: a sourced Turlock commercial-rent figure becomes available
iteration_protocol.action: re-pair the revenue bands with the occupancy load and refresh the margin reality

iteration_protocol.trigger: a surrounding-town or Modesto format-mix shift, or a trade-area capture study
iteration_protocol.action: re-derive the two-way destination pull and the leakage ranking

iteration_protocol.trigger: a national independent-specialty store-per-capita benchmark updates
iteration_protocol.action: re-frame the density comparator and re-state the modest-not-saturated read

priority_rationale: The discretionary demand base, the ethnic life-event economy and the coverage floor are foundational because density, the revenue bands, saturation and white-space all read from them; the saturation density and per-sub-category bands precede the margin reality and the competitive/lopsidedness reads they constrain; competitive structure, the capex/skill and regulatory gates, leakage and online pressure build on the demand and band layers; the income cap, event-volume ceiling and two-way destination pull contextualize the saturation reads; the revenue-honesty guardrail governs every dollar expression; and the go/no-go verdict plus the review loop come last because they compose all upstream reads into a decision and a self-correcting refresh.
